witness.text:
a
$300,000 mortgage seem manageable at

comparisons.rationale: A $1,500 payment on $300,000 over 30 years implies about 4.4%, while the 30-year rate in the week of the registry upload date (11 September 2025) was 6.35%, giving $1,867; if "$300,000 mortgage" means a $300,000 house with 20% down, the loan is $240,000 and $1,493 at 6.35% would match, so the figure is outdated or ambiguous depending on the meaning. The later interest-share check uses 6.5%; at the video's implied 4.4% the first-decade interest share would be about 66% rather than 80%.
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic recomputed; FRED MORTGAGE30US fetched this session; the upload date is taken from the registry; the meaning of "$300,000 mortgage" is not stated.

witness.text:
that monthly payment

comparisons.rationale: The spoken claims conflict with each other: doubling $1,500 gives $3,000, about 78% of take-home on $55,000 gross, above the stated "60 to 70%"; add-ons of 40-60% of the base (analyst estimate, unsourced) give $2,100-$2,400, which is 55-62% of take-home.
